category_title: Students exhibiting off-task 'silly' behavior and peer-directed inappropriate gestures
minimal_context: The student is working on an analog spelling task that requires putting words in alphabetical order and writing them multiple times in the general classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our spelling activity. Please place the words from your list in alphabetical order and write them three times each on your paper.

STUDENT: (Stares at the blank paper and begins making a low humming noise instead of picking up the pencil.)

TUTOR: Keep trying, you need to write the words down.

STUDENT: (Writes one word, then turns around in his seat to face a peer, making a silly face and talking inappropriately to them.)

TUTOR: Please face forward and start making up sentences using the words.

STUDENT: (Ignores the instruction to write sentences, makes loud animal noises, and begins directing inappropriate hand gestures toward the peer sitting next to him.)

options.A: Have the student use a digital application like Evernote to take notes, organize their spelling work, and archive past word lists and sentences.
options.B: Have the student alphabetize words for a few minutes, write sentences for a few minutes, and then participate in a class discussion and partner share.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each part of the spelling activity, such as alphabetizing the words and writing them on the paper.
options.D: Have the student make a crossword puzzle using the words from the spelling list, explaining in advance that the puzzle will be completed by another student.
